messages:
jess: Getting reports that SCIM pushes from our idp-sync job are failing with 401s. Started ~09:07 UTC. Anyone seen this? :confused:
vik: Seen it in monitoring  alert: scim-provisioner 5xx/401 spike. Grabbing logs now.
sam: Throwing top log snippet: 
```
2026-04-02T09:07:11Z WARN scim-client.go:88 token fetch failed: invalid_token: Token validation failed: invalid_audience (aud: https://console.redwood.com, expected: api://scim)
http request: POST /scim/v2/Users
response: 401 Unauthorized
```
jess: That aud mismatch looks like the OIDC client is requesting tokens for the console audience instead of the scim API. Did we change client_id or audience mapping in the oauth-proxy rollout?
vik: There was a small change in idp-config earlier today that updated allowed-audiences for the oauth client: https://git.redwood.com/r/redwood/idp-config/commit/3f9a2a. It added `console` to the allowed list but I don't see scim listed explicitly.
oncall: Okta logs show token issued with aud: ["https://console.redwood.com"]. The client was using client_id: redwood-oauth (shared). Maybe a duplicate client was created in prod for the console?
sam: I queried our token-exchange lambda and it requests audience from env var TARGET_AUD. In the prod lambda config it's set to `https://console.redwood.com` (looks like dev->prod mistake). 
```
aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name token-exchange-prod
# -> Environment.Variables.TARGET_AUD=https://console.redwood.com
```
jess: Ok, that's probably the root cause. SCIM expects token with aud `api://scim`. Because aud mismatch token validation fails upstream and provisioner rejects.
vik: Mitigation: 1) update lambda env to correct audience, 2) restart provisioner pods so they request fresh tokens, 3) pause scheduled idp-sync job to avoid retries until we confirm.
oncall: Also seeing some RBAC role-mapping alerts: a recent RBAC change trimmed role claim values (we had a truncation bug of 64->32 chars) so some users lost mapped roles and were scheduled for bulk reassignments via SCIM. That combined with the token failures is causing noisy retries.
sam: Nice catch. Which PR introduced the truncation? I see PR 502 in idp-services changed the claim serializer.
vik: Correct, PR: https://git.redwood.com/r/redwood/idp-services/pulls/502. I opened a rollback PR to restore full-length claim handling: https://git.redwood.com/r/redwood/idp-services/pulls/504
jess: Immediate actions I'm taking now: 
- pausing CronJob idp-sync: `kubectl -n idp-prod patch cronjob idp-sync -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`
- update lambda env var to `api://scim` and publish new version
- create an allowlist block in scim-provisioner for current retry window to ignore duplicate deletes

sam: I'll roll the oauth token-exchange lambda change now. Pushing patch -> publish.

idp-bot: Runbook step triggered: 'OIDC audience mismatch' runbook linked: https://runbooks.redwood.com/oidc-aud-mismatch. Adding pointer to incident.

security-bot: Creating incident INC-2026-045: SCIM token audience mismatch causing provisioning 401s and RBAC mapping drift. Notifying oncall.

oncall: Acknowledged. Coordinating with Customer Success on user-facing impact.

vik: Lambda env updated to api://scim and new version published (v12). Rolling token-exchange deployment to 2 instances for canary.

sam: Restarted 1 provisioner pod to pick up new token flow: `kubectl -n idp-prod rollout restart deployment/scim-provisioner -n idp-prod --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rolledAt":"$(date +%s)"}}}}}'`

sam: After restart, provisioner fetched token with aud api://scim and a test user create succeeded (201 Created).

jess: Good. Next: merge rollback for claim truncation, redeploy idp-services, and then unpause cronjob after small canary run. Also add an extra validation in provisioner to log the token aud on fetch so we can detect this earlier.

vik: Agreed. I'll also add an alert that triggers when token aud != expected for >1 minute.

sam: Tracking issues created: TRACK-1188 (aud validation alert), TRACK-1189 (dead-letter queue for failed SCIM ops), TRACK-1190 (claim-serializer fix).

jess: Quick note for postmortem: update KMS/secret rotation runbook? Not directly related here but ensure secret rotations don't coincide with client config changes (reduce blast radius).

security-bot: Reminder: attach Okta token logs and audit entries to INC-2026-045 when you close the incident.

oncall: CS notified, no major user-facing outages reported yet. Will monitor for 60m and then gradually resume backfills.

jess: Thanks all. I'll post the postmortem draft after we close the incident.
